outcomeNote: One amoraic teaching on the mishna's clause, with its prooftext; nothing is contested.

segments.he: וּרְקִיקָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר. אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הָרוֹקֵק בְּהַר הַבַּיִת בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה, כְּאִילּוּ רוֹקֵק בְּבַת עֵינוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהָיוּ עֵינַי וְלִבִּי שָׁם כָּל הַיָּמִים״.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna that «spitting» on the Temple Mount is prohibited «through an a fortiori inference. Rav Beivai said» that «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Anyone who spits on the Temple Mount,» even «today, it is as if he spit in the pupil of» God’s «eye, as it is stated: “And My eyes and My heart shall be there perpetually”» (I Kings 9:3).
